findings.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex lets two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource proceed in parallel, because the lock now only guards the final cache write. Two goroutines (e.g., two simultaneous search requests for the same namespace/resource during cold start) both miss the cache, both call bleve.New on the same directory when size > FileThreshold, and the second one fails with a lock/exists error on the bleve index dir, returning a 500 search failure that the previous serialized construction could not produce; in-memory indexes are also built twice, doubling startup CPU and memory.

[BUG] Init's initialization work (per the surrounding code, s.initErr is assigned inside a goroutine that runs asynchronously) is now checked exactly once in the constructor, and every per-request `s.Init(ctx)` error check has been deleted, so a background init failure is never surfaced to callers again. When the background search-index init or initWatcher fails after NewResourceServer returns nil error, Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search all proceed against a half-initialized server (no watcher running, missing/stale index) and return wrong-but-plausible results instead of the error they previously returned via the per-request Init check.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init from lazy per-first-request into the constructor converts every NewResourceServer call into a blocking full search-index build, and the diff simultaneously skips the postgres integration test rather than fixing it. Any process or test that constructs a ResourceServer (including Drone CI on postgres, per the added skip) now blocks startup on index building and fails on init errors that were previously deferred to first request; the postgres skip comment 'test not working with postgres in Drone' is direct evidence the eager init broke a real environment and was masked instead of diagnosed, leaving an uncovered regression path with zero test coverage.

[BUG] The new `s.Init(ctx)` call in NewResourceServer references a `ctx` that the diff never shows being defined in that function's scope or parameter list. If NewResourceServer's signature (not shown in the hunks) was not updated to accept a context, this is a compile-time failure of the package; if it was updated, every existing caller in the repo and in downstream embedders must now supply a ctx, which the diff shows no call-site updates for.

[ADVISORY] The new startup log line calls s.search.TotalDocs(), a method that must exist on the search backend type but is not introduced anywhere in this diff. If TotalDocs is not already defined on the backend interface/struct used by searchSupport, the package fails to compile; even if it exists, the log fires inside init before the builder goroutine shown at line ~213 has finished, so it logs total_docs before documents are indexed, misleading anyone debugging slow startup.

[BUG] Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) drops write events that occur during index construction, leaving the search index permanently stale for those resources. A dashboard created/updated while the initial index build is running (builds take seconds-to-minutes on large tenants, as the init log of duration_secs shows) is never written to the index because no watcher is registered yet; the event has no WrittenEvent record and is not replayed, so Search returns stale/missing results until a full restart reindexes.

[ADVISORY] Moving lazy Init() out of every RPC handler into NewResourceServer converts per-request initialization failure into a hard construction-time failure. Any transient backend error during startup (search index build, watcher registration) now fails NewResourceServer and blocks Grafana startup entirely, where previously the server would construct successfully and each RPC would retry Init; operators on flaky storage get a downed instance instead of degraded requests.

[BUG] Narrowing cacheMu in BuildIndex from the whole call to just the cache write removes the mutual exclusion that previously serialized concurrent index builds, so concurrent builders for the same key race on the bleve directory and cache entry. searchSupport.init builds in a spawned goroutine (init returns while building continues per the `}()` before the duration log) while handleEvent can call getOrCreateIndex concurrently; two BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource both pass the nil-cache check, both write the same on-disk bleve directory (file-threshold path), and one index instance is silently discarded, so events applied to the discarded index are lost from search results.

[ADVISORY] The diff permanently skips the only integration test covering the resource server on postgres with a 'TODO - fix this test' comment, removing all CI verification of the exact code paths this PR changes. The Init-reordering, eager-init-in-NewResourceServer, and bleve lock changes in this PR ship with zero postgres CI coverage — the environment where SQL-backend init behavior actually differs — so regressions in Init ordering or startup failure modes on postgres will not be caught before release.

[ADVISORY] Removing the Init() guard from Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, and GetBlob leaves these RPCs calling s.search, s.diagnostics, and s.blob without any initialization guarantee when a ResourceServer is constructed by any path other than NewResourceServer. Any caller constructing the server via a different constructor or test harness that invokes Init lazily (the public Init method is retained, implying external use) now hits nil-pointer or empty-state panics on these handlers; the retained public Init surface combined with removed internal call sites is a silent contract change for out-of-tree constructors.

[BUG] Reordering init so the search index build completes before initWatcher starts means writes that occur during the (potentially minutes-long) initial index build are never captured, leaving documents permanently missing from the search index until a full rebuild. Any resource created/updated between the index snapshot and watcher start is invisible to Search/History for that tenant indefinitely; previously the watcher was started first so those events were buffered and replayed onto the index.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from around the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key to run simultaneously, and the last writer to b.cache[key] wins regardless of which build had the fresher data. Concurrent getOrCreateIndex misses for the same key each build a full Bleve index (duplicate CPU/memory spike), and if the older-RV build finishes last it overwrites the cache entry, serving a stale index with no error signal; the previous global lock serialized this and made the first build authoritative.

[ADVISORY] Init is now invoked exactly once from NewResourceServer with whatever context the constructor was handed, and every per-request Init call was deleted, so the Init guard exists in only one path. Any code that constructs the server without going through NewResourceServer (tests or embedded use building the struct directly, as this package's own tests have historically done) gets a server whose watcher/search index were never initialized; every method that previously self-healed now silently operates on an empty index, and there is no runtime assertion that init ran.

[ADVISORY] The watcher and search-index background loops now inherit the context passed into NewResourceServer rather than a context owned by the server's lifetime. If the caller passes a request-scoped or otherwise cancellable context to the constructor, the watcher and index event consumer are cancelled the moment that context is done, and because no method re-runs Init anymore, the server serves stale data for the rest of the process lifetime with no log at the call sites that removed the Init guard.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.'), so the changed unified-storage server path (which now runs Init in the constructor) is never exercised against postgres in CI. CI goes green while the postgres storage-server path is unverified; the exact constructor-time Init change in this diff could fail only under postgres and the suite would not catch it, deferring discovery to production or an operator running locally.

[ADVISORY] The high-index-latency warning compares latencySeconds (computed from microsecond-precision time.Now().UnixMicro()) against a bare literal 5, and now routes through s.log.Warn — but the warning fires per-event with no aggregation or downstream action. Operators on a lagging deployment get one warn line per written event (potentially thousands per minute) with no rate limiting, drowning real log signal; the magic number 5 seconds is also undocumented as to whether it is a p99 target or an alerting threshold.

[ADVISORY] Init moved from lazy per-request to eager constructor invocation, converting every previously-recoverable per-request initialization failure into a hard NewResourceServer failure. Operators running the unified storage server against a degraded backend (e.g., search index build fails due to a transient DB error) now get a process that refuses to start instead of a server that serves requests and returns errors only on the affected calls; anyone relying on the previous degraded-but-up behavior gets a full outage, and this objective change (availability semantics) was not explicitly accepted as part of a 'performance optimizations' PR.

[ADVISORY] initWatcher is now invoked after search index initialization instead of before, so writes occurring during a long index build are never delivered to the watcher and never re-indexed. With the old ordering the watcher was live before the index built, capturing events during the build window; after this reorder, any resource written while the initial index build runs (which can take many seconds on large tenants — the diff even adds a duration_secs log) is silently missing from the search index, producing stale search results for those documents until a full rebuild. Because Init now also runs synchronously in the constructor, the build window is on the startup path, guaranteeing real traffic in multi-replica rolling deploys hits it.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is permanently skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.') and no tracking issue or fix plan. The unified storage server's integration coverage on postgres — the primary production database for Grafana — is now zero, so regressions introduced by this very PR's constructor-time Init change (which the diff acknowledges is broken on Drone/postgres) will not be caught by CI; whoever eventually touches this code inherits an unexplained, unreproducible-in-CI failure. Silent test deletion inside a performance PR is a constraint change (postgres is now effectively unsupported by CI) that was never explicitly accepted.

[ADVISORY] Removing the full-duration cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows two concurrent builds for the same key to both construct indexes, with the second cache write overwriting the first while callers of the first index keep a stale object. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex misses (e.g., two simultaneous Search requests for a cold resource after startup-init races) now each build a full bleve index; the loser's in-memory handle diverges from the cache, so events applied via the cached index are invisible to the holder of the overwritten one and vice versa, producing inconsistent search results and duplicated memory/file handles (two bleve indexes on the same on-disk directory when above FileThreshold, where the loser also holds an open file index). Previously the mutex serialized builds, making this impossible.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init into NewResourceServer converts a per-request lazy initialization failure into a hard construction failure while all per-method Init guards are deleted. If the search index build or watcher startup fails (e.g. transient DB unavailability, disk full for the bleve file index), the resource server cannot be constructed at all, taking the whole storage server down at startup; previously these paths served degraded-but-alive. Operators get a crash-loop instead of a degraded subsystem, and any caller that ignores the returned error uses a nil *server and panics.

[ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu hold for the duration of BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to both complete full index builds, with the second writer overwriting the first's entry in b.cache. During concurrent first-access initialization of the same NamespacedResource, CPU and memory are double-spent on full bleve index builds, and an index handle already handed to a reader via the first store is silently orphaned (its documents never receive watcher updates since the watcher is registered against whichever instance the second call returns), producing a stale/un-updating search index for that resource until restart. The final map write is locked, but the check-then-build-then-publish sequence is not atomic.

[ADVISORY] The diff disables the only postgres coverage of the instrumentation-server integration path by unconditionally skipping the test. CI (Drone) now runs this integration test against no database backend at all (sqlite skipped, postgres skipped), so regressions in the resource server's integration wiring — including the new eager-init-in-constructor behavior introduced in this same PR — will pass CI while breaking postgres deployments; the TODO comment signals this is deferred, not fixed, and the skip has no tracking issue or expiry.

[ADVISORY] The diff changes the server's initialization lifecycle from lazy per-request Init to eager init inside NewResourceServer, with no test modification verifying the new path — the only test change in this diff is a skip. The new failure mode (NewResourceServer returning an error and blocking startup when search index init fails, where previously each RPC would have returned a per-request error) has no coverage: no test constructs a server with a failing search backend, and no test verifies RPC handlers (Read/List/Watch/Search) still succeed after the lazy Init calls were stripped from them. A regression where Init is dropped or duplicated (e.g. the handler previously depended on Init's side effects like the context values) would pass the existing suite. Checked: the only test-shaped file in this diff is pkg/server/module_server_test.go, which only adds skips and contains no assertions about init behavior.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes the serialization of BuildIndex (cacheMu held for the whole build is narrowed to only the cache write) with no test exercising concurrent BuildIndex calls. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key now both proceed past the removed lock and can create two bleve indexes (two writers to the same on-disk directory when size > FileThreshold), with the loser's index silently overwriting the winner in b.cache and a possible file-handle conflict on the persistent directory. The only test files in this diff (pkg/server/module_server_test.go) do not touch bleve.go, and no other spec exercises concurrent BuildIndex; the concurrency guarantee changed by this diff is entirely unverified.

[ADVISORY] The diff reorders init so search index build completes before initWatcher starts, but no test verifies the ordering dependency this reordering implies. If the ordering is wrong (events dropped between index build and watcher start, or watcher events racing the initial build), no test in the diff detects it — the only test change is the postgres skip, and an integration test asserting that documents created just before/after startup are searchable would be required to catch a missed-event regression, which CI now never runs on postgres.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex leaves the b.cache map read (early in the function) unprotected while other goroutines write b.cache[key] = idx, causing a concurrent map read/write panic. During startup, getOrCreateIndex fans out one BuildIndex call per NamespacedResource concurrently; two of those racing (one reading the cache, one completing and writing b.cache[key]) trigger Go's fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' runtime panic, crashing the storage server during index initialization.

[BUG] Reordering Init so the search index is fully built before initWatcher() starts means writes committed to the SQL backend during the (potentially minutes-long) index build are never delivered to the index, leaving it permanently stale for those keys. A dashboard saved while init is still building indexes produces no watcher event for that snapshot; the search index serves stale/missing results for that resource until a full reindex or another write to the same key occurs, so users see outdated search results after the very startup this diff slows down with the now-synchronous Init.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init() from lazy per-request initialization into NewResourceServer converts every previously-tolerable per-request init failure into a hard construction failure for the whole process. Operators of deployments where the search index build intermittently fails (transient DB error, bleve file lock on a shared volume) previously kept serving Create/Read/List while Search degraded; after this diff the resource server fails to construct and the entire unified-storage server refuses to start, turning a partial degradation into a full outage.

[BUG] History() and Origin() now call s.search.History/s.search.Origin with the Init guard removed and, unlike Search(), carry no s.search == nil check, so a server constructed without a search backend panics on these methods. Any deployment configured without the search backend (search only wired when opts.SearchBackend is set) receives a nil-pointer dereference on the History/Origin RPCs instead of the previous error path, crashing the request handler where the pre-diff Init-guarded flow did not dereference nil.

[BUG] Moving initWatcher() to run after search.init() opens an unobserved-write window: search.init() builds the index from a DB snapshot, and any writes committed after that snapshot but before initWatcher() starts are never delivered to the index. Resources created/updated while a large index is building (the exact time index building is slow) are permanently missing from the search index until the next restart or rebuild — searches silently return stale results with no error surfaced anywhere; previously the watcher was registered first, so events during the build were captured.

[ADVISORY] Init() is now invoked only from NewResourceServer, converting what was a per-request lazy failure into a hard process-startup failure while the Init() method itself is retained and still public. Operators of deployments where search index init transiently fails (slow DB during startup) now get a server that refuses to boot rather than serving degraded CRUD while retrying init; and any future/alternate constructor path that builds a `server` value without going through NewResourceServer silently serves requests against an uninitialized server (no Init call, no error, watcher never started).

[ADVISORY] Removing the whole-function cacheMu lock from BuildIndex removes the in-flight guard that prevented two concurrent builds for the same key, leaving only the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write protected. Concurrent callers of getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource (e.g., two search requests racing on a cold index) each run a full builder pass against the database and both create a bleve index; the loser's index object is silently discarded and never closed, leaking file handles/memory on the file-backed path, and the winner may be overwritten by the later-finishing stale build (last-write-wins), so searches can serve the older index with no error.

[ADVISORY] On the file-backed path, if the builder callback or any step after `bleve.New(dir, ...)` succeeds but a later step returns an error, the created on-disk bleve index is never closed or cleaned up. Repeated failed builds leave orphaned index directories and open file descriptors under b.opts.Root; the pre-existing `size > FileThreshold` check means large tenants hit this on every retry, eventually exhausting file handles on the server.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show per-request `s.Init(ctx)` checks removed from many RPC handlers and an `s.Init(ctx)` call added in `NewResourceServer` (server.go). However, the finding’s core claim depends on `Init` doing its work asynchronously in a goroutine and returning nil before `s.initErr` is set. No goroutine/asynchronous behavior is shown in the diff hunks; the visible `Init` code appears synchronous (it sets `s.initErr` and logs within the same control flow). From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that an init failure can occur “after NewResourceServer returns” and thus be hidden from callers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization from lazy per-RPC calls (removed `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) to eager initialization in `NewResourceServer` (`err := s.Init(ctx)` before returning). `Init` runs `s.search.init(ctx)` when search is configured, which can be a heavy/blocking operation and now makes construction fail-fast on init errors rather than deferring to first request. Separately, the integration test is explicitly skipped for postgres with a comment about Drone CI, reducing coverage for the environment most likely to expose the issue. The finding’s core concern (startup/constructor now blocks on init + regression path masked by skipping postgres) is grounded in the diff, though whether it is an outright defect vs. an intentional behavior change is not provable from the diff alone.

If there isn’t a `ctx := ...` earlier in `NewResourceServer` outside the hunk, this would be a compile-time error due to `ctx` being undefined.

In the same function, the diff shows a `go func() { ... }()` launched just before this log, meaning the log can run before that goroutine completes, so `total_docs` (and the message "initialized") may reflect a partially built/empty index and be misleading. The claim that `TotalDocs()` is missing and would fail compilation is not verifiable from this diff alone (the method/interface definition isn’t shown).

This changes failure mode from “server constructs and each request attempts Init (potentially retrying)” to “server construction fails and can block startup if Init (search init/watcher) errors.” That’s a real, diff-grounded behavioral/operational concern, but not provably an incorrectness bug by itself (could be an intentional design choice).

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` used to hold `b.cacheMu` for the entire call; the diff narrows locking to only the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. That means two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `NamespacedResource` can both proceed past any cache state and concurrently execute `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk directory (`dir := filepath.Join(...)` when `size > FileThreshold`), which is not mutually excluded by the new code. The diff also shows `searchSupport.init` spawns work in a goroutine (`go func(){ ... }()`), so index building can overlap with other activity (e.g., watcher/event handling calling into index creation), making such concurrent builds plausible. This is a correctness/data-consistency risk introduced by the lock change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: search index init (`s.search.init(ctx)`) now runs before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started first. That change can plausibly create a gap where writes occurring during a long-running index build are not observed by the watcher. However, the diff does not show how `initWatcher` works (e.g., whether it starts from a specific resource version, replays a backlog, or whether `search.init` builds from a consistent snapshot), so the claim that documents are "permanently missing" is not directly verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from around the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key to run simultaneously, and the last writer to b.cache[key] wins regardless of which build had the fresher data. Concurrent getOrCreateIndex misses for the same key each build a full Bleve index (duplicate CPU/memory spike), and if the older-RV build finishes last it overwrites the cache entry, serving a stale index with no error signal; the previous global lock serialized this and made the first build authoritative.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function; the diff removes that global lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. There is no diff-visible per-key/singleflight guard or RV freshness check before overwriting the cache. Therefore, if BuildIndex is invoked concurrently for the same `key` (which is plausible in a server), both will build full indexes and the last finisher will overwrite `b.cache[key]` regardless of which `rv` is newer, potentially serving a stale index.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init is now invoked exactly once from NewResourceServer with whatever context the constructor was handed, and every per-request Init call was deleted, so the Init guard exists in only one path. Any code that constructs the server without going through NewResourceServer (tests or embedded use building the struct directly, as this package's own tests have historically done) gets a server whose watcher/search index were never initialized; every method that previously self-healed now silently operates on an empty index, and there is no runtime assertion that init ran.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` once (server.go:255+) and all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob`. This makes initialization dependent on construction via `NewResourceServer`; if any code builds `server` without that constructor, none of these methods will trigger init anymore. The diff does not prove such usages exist, so it’s not a verifiable defect, but it is a concrete, change-induced robustness/usage-contract concern grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The watcher and search-index background loops now inherit the context passed into NewResourceServer rather than a context owned by the server's lifetime. If the caller passes a request-scoped or otherwise cancellable context to the constructor, the watcher and index event consumer are cancelled the moment that context is done, and because no method re-runs Init anymore, the server serves stale data for the rest of the process lifetime with no log at the call sites that removed the Init guard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move `Init(ctx)` from per-RPC methods into `NewResourceServer()` and removes the guards in `Create/Update/...`, but `Init` is protected by `s.initOnce.Do(...)` so it would never have been “re-run” on later calls anyway. Also, any `ctx` cancellation during initialization now causes `NewResourceServer` to return an error (it logs and returns `nil, err`), so the “server serves stale data for the rest of the process lifetime” claim is not supported by what’s shown. The diff does not demonstrate that the watcher/search loops are tied to a request-scoped constructor context in a way that would silently cancel them after successful init.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.'), so the changed unified-storage server path (which now runs Init in the constructor) is never exercised against postgres in CI. CI goes green while the postgres storage-server path is unverified; the exact constructor-time Init change in this diff could fail only under postgres and the suite would not catch it, deferring discovery to production or an operator running locally.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres skip in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a TODO noting it fails in Drone, so that integration test will not run under postgres in CI. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` is changed to call `s.Init(ctx)` at construction time (and removes per-RPC `Init` calls), which is a nontrivial behavioral change that could plausibly surface DB-specific issues. While the diff cannot prove CI would otherwise exercise postgres for this path, the added skip does reduce postgres coverage for this integration test around the changed initialization behavior, making this a concrete, diff-grounded test-gap concern rather than a confirmed bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The high-index-latency warning compares latencySeconds (computed from microsecond-precision time.Now().UnixMicro()) against a bare literal 5, and now routes through s.log.Warn — but the warning fires per-event with no aggregation or downstream action. Operators on a lagging deployment get one warn line per written event (potentially thousands per minute) with no rate limiting, drowning real log signal; the magic number 5 seconds is also undocumented as to whether it is a p99 target or an alerting threshold.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go::handleEvent(), the code computes latencySeconds and logs a warning for every event when latencySeconds > 5 (a bare literal) via s.log.Warn("high index latency", ...). The diff explicitly changes the logger call (from logger.Warn to s.log.Warn) but keeps the per-event, unthrottled behavior and the undocumented 5-second threshold, which can plausibly spam logs on lagging deployments. This is an operational/observability concern rather than a correctness defect, and it is directly grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init moved from lazy per-request to eager constructor invocation, converting every previously-recoverable per-request initialization failure into a hard NewResourceServer failure. Operators running the unified storage server against a degraded backend (e.g., search index build fails due to a transient DB error) now get a process that refuses to start instead of a server that serves requests and returns errors only on the affected calls; anyone relying on the previous degraded-but-up behavior gets a full outage, and this objective change (availability semantics) was not explicitly accepted as part of a 'performance optimizations' PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an explicit semantic change: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (server.go @@255+), and the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` (many hunks). This makes initialization failures (e.g., `s.search.init(ctx)` inside `Init`) prevent server construction/startup rather than surfacing only when a request hits the server, which is an availability/behavior change that should be explicitly accepted even if not strictly a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] initWatcher is now invoked after search index initialization instead of before, so writes occurring during a long index build are never delivered to the watcher and never re-indexed. With the old ordering the watcher was live before the index built, capturing events during the build window; after this reorder, any resource written while the initial index build runs (which can take many seconds on large tenants — the diff even adds a duration_secs log) is silently missing from the search index, producing stale search results for those documents until a full rebuild. Because Init now also runs synchronously in the constructor, the build window is on the startup path, guaranteeing real traffic in multi-replica rolling deploys hits it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably reorder initialization in `server.Init`: search index initialization (`s.search.init(ctx)`) now runs before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started first (see the moved blocks in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`). The diff also makes `NewResourceServer` call `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously on construction and removes per-RPC `Init` calls, increasing the likelihood that traffic overlaps with any long-running init. However, the claim that writes during the build window are "never delivered" and therefore "silently missing from the search index" cannot be proven from this diff alone because the behavior of `initWatcher()` and the search build process (e.g., whether the watcher can start from a resource version / replay backlog) is not shown. So this is a concrete, diff-grounded ordering/regression risk, but not a verifiable defect from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is permanently skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.') and no tracking issue or fix plan. The unified storage server's integration coverage on postgres — the primary production database for Grafana — is now zero, so regressions introduced by this very PR's constructor-time Init change (which the diff acknowledges is broken on Drone/postgres) will not be caught by CI; whoever eventually touches this code inherits an unexplained, unreproducible-in-CI failure. Silent test deletion inside a performance PR is a constraint change (postgres is now effectively unsupported by CI) that was never explicitly accepted.

[ADVISORY] Removing the full-duration cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows two concurrent builds for the same key to both construct indexes, with the second cache write overwriting the first while callers of the first index keep a stale object. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex misses (e.g., two simultaneous Search requests for a cold resource after startup-init races) now each build a full bleve index; the loser's in-memory handle diverges from the cache, so events applied via the cached index are invisible to the holder of the overwritten one and vice versa, producing inconsistent search results and duplicated memory/file handles (two bleve indexes on the same on-disk directory when above FileThreshold, where the loser also holds an open file index). Previously the mutex serialized builds, making this impossible.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` previously held `b.cacheMu` for the entire build (`b.cacheMu.Lock(); defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()`), but the diff removes that and now only locks briefly around `b.cache[key] = idx`. Since the index path is deterministic per `key` (e.g., `filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", key.Resource, key.Group))`), two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same key can both proceed to construct separate Bleve indexes (or race on the same on-disk directory) and then race on the final cache write, with the later write overwriting the earlier. Any caller that received the earlier `idx` can then hold an index handle that diverges from what future lookups/events use via the cache, leading to inconsistent indexing/search behavior and duplicated open handles. The diff itself removes the only shown serialization that prevented this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving Init into NewResourceServer converts a per-request lazy initialization failure into a hard construction failure while all per-method Init guards are deleted. If the search index build or watcher startup fails (e.g. transient DB unavailability, disk full for the bleve file index), the resource server cannot be constructed at all, taking the whole storage server down at startup; previously these paths served degraded-but-alive. Operators get a crash-loop instead of a degraded subsystem, and any caller that ignores the returned error uses a nil *server and panics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (server.go: NewResourceServer), while the per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); ...` guards were removed from many methods (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This does convert initialization errors in `Init` (which runs `s.search.init(ctx)` and `s.initWatcher()`) into a construction-time failure rather than a first-request failure. The claim about callers ignoring the returned error and panicking is not verifiable from this diff (no call sites shown), and the “previously served degraded-but-alive” aspect is arguable since RPCs previously returned an error when `Init` failed, but the operational/architecture concern about startup hard-failing is grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu hold for the duration of BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to both complete full index builds, with the second writer overwriting the first's entry in b.cache. During concurrent first-access initialization of the same NamespacedResource, CPU and memory are double-spent on full bleve index builds, and an index handle already handed to a reader via the first store is silently orphaned (its documents never receive watcher updates since the watcher is registered against whichever instance the second call returns), producing a stale/un-updating search index for that resource until restart. The final map write is locked, but the check-then-build-then-publish sequence is not atomic.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (build + publish). The diff removes that long-held lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. Since there is no check for an existing `b.cache[key]` entry in this function, two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` can both build full indexes concurrently and then race to publish, with the later call overwriting the earlier cache entry. This makes the check/build/publish sequence non-atomic and can lead to wasted work and inconsistent cached index selection under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff disables the only postgres coverage of the instrumentation-server integration path by unconditionally skipping the test. CI (Drone) now runs this integration test against no database backend at all (sqlite skipped, postgres skipped), so regressions in the resource server's integration wiring — including the new eager-init-in-constructor behavior introduced in this same PR — will pass CI while breaking postgres deployments; the TODO comment signals this is deferred, not fixed, and the skip has no tracking issue or expiry.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip(...) }`), and the test already skips sqlite (`if dbType == "sqlite3" { t.Skip(...) }`). From the diff, this reduces/possibly eliminates DB-backed coverage of that integration path (including the new eager `s.Init(ctx)` call in `NewResourceServer`), with only a TODO comment and no in-code tracking/expiry. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test/coverage regression rather than a direct product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff changes the server's initialization lifecycle from lazy per-request Init to eager init inside NewResourceServer, with no test modification verifying the new path — the only test change in this diff is a skip. The new failure mode (NewResourceServer returning an error and blocking startup when search index init fails, where previously each RPC would have returned a per-request error) has no coverage: no test constructs a server with a failing search backend, and no test verifies RPC handlers (Read/List/Watch/Search) still succeed after the lazy Init calls were stripped from them. A regression where Init is dropped or duplicated (e.g. the handler previously depended on Init's side effects like the context values) would pass the existing suite. Checked: the only test-shaped file in this diff is pkg/server/module_server_test.go, which only adds skips and contains no assertions about init behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and the per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from many handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). The only test change shown is adding skips in pkg/server/module_server_test.go, with no new assertions covering the eager-init path or failure mode. While not a provable defect by itself, it is a concrete, diff-grounded risk/coverage gap for the new lifecycle behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff removes the serialization of BuildIndex (cacheMu held for the whole build is narrowed to only the cache write) with no test exercising concurrent BuildIndex calls. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key now both proceed past the removed lock and can create two bleve indexes (two writers to the same on-disk directory when size > FileThreshold), with the loser's index silently overwriting the winner in b.cache and a possible file-handle conflict on the persistent directory. The only test files in this diff (pkg/server/module_server_test.go) do not touch bleve.go, and no other spec exercises concurrent BuildIndex; the concurrency guarantee changed by this diff is entirely unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (covering index creation and building). The diff removes that broad lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This changes the concurrency guarantee: two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` can both execute `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`, potentially creating/opening the same on-disk directory concurrently and racing to store different `idx` values into `b.cache`. The diff does not add any alternative per-key serialization here, and the only test change is unrelated (skipping a DB integration test), so this behavioral change is unverified in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff reorders init so search index build completes before initWatcher starts, but no test verifies the ordering dependency this reordering implies. If the ordering is wrong (events dropped between index build and watcher start, or watcher events racing the initial build), no test in the diff detects it — the only test change is the postgres skip, and an integration test asserting that documents created just before/after startup are searchable would be required to catch a missed-event regression, which CI now never runs on postgres.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization: in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Init(), the search index init (s.search.init(ctx)) now runs before starting the watcher (s.initWatcher()), whereas previously watcher startup happened first. That can change behavior around events occurring during startup, and the diff adds no test covering the ordering-sensitive scenario described; the only test change is skipping postgres in module_server_test.go. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-gap/behavior-risk, but not a provable defect solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex leaves the b.cache map read (early in the function) unprotected while other goroutines write b.cache[key] = idx, causing a concurrent map read/write panic. During startup, getOrCreateIndex fans out one BuildIndex call per NamespacedResource concurrently; two of those racing (one reading the cache, one completing and writing b.cache[key]) trigger Go's fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' runtime panic, crashing the storage server during index initialization.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff for `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, the only shown access to `b.cache` inside `BuildIndex` is the write `b.cache[key] = idx`, which is now explicitly protected by `b.cacheMu.Lock()/Unlock()`. The finding’s claim that `BuildIndex` performs an *early, unprotected read* of `b.cache` is not verifiable from the provided diff hunk (no such read is shown), so the specific concurrent map read/write panic scenario cannot be confirmed from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering Init so the search index is fully built before initWatcher() starts means writes committed to the SQL backend during the (potentially minutes-long) index build are never delivered to the index, leaving it permanently stale for those keys. A dashboard saved while init is still building indexes produces no watcher event for that snapshot; the search index serves stale/missing results for that resource until a full reindex or another write to the same key occurs, so users see outdated search results after the very startup this diff slows down with the now-synchronous Init.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go explicitly reorders initialization so `s.search.init(ctx)` runs before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). If the watcher is responsible for delivering subsequent writes/updates to the search index, this creates a window during the potentially long index build where changes committed to the backend can occur without any watcher running to observe and index them. Nothing in the shown diff indicates a catch-up/replay mechanism after `search.init` to reconcile changes that happened during the build, so the finding’s core risk (missed updates leading to a stale index) is grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving Init() from lazy per-request initialization into NewResourceServer converts every previously-tolerable per-request init failure into a hard construction failure for the whole process. Operators of deployments where the search index build intermittently fails (transient DB error, bleve file lock on a shared volume) previously kept serving Create/Read/List while Search degraded; after this diff the resource server fails to construct and the entire unified-storage server refuses to start, turning a partial degradation into a full outage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization to construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (server.go). Previously `Init(ctx)` was called lazily in every RPC handler (Create/Read/List/Search/etc.), and those calls were removed. This does change the failure mode from “process starts but first request triggers init error” to “resource server fails to construct/start if init fails”. However, the finding’s claim that operators could previously keep serving Create/Read/List while Search degraded is not supported by the diff, because `Init` included search index initialization and its error would have been returned by all handlers that called `Init`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] History() and Origin() now call s.search.History/s.search.Origin with the Init guard removed and, unlike Search(), carry no s.search == nil check, so a server constructed without a search backend panics on these methods. Any deployment configured without the search backend (search only wired when opts.SearchBackend is set) receives a nil-pointer dereference on the History/Origin RPCs instead of the previous error path, crashing the request handler where the pre-diff Init-guarded flow did not dereference nil.

adjudication.rationale: In server.go, History() and Origin() now directly call `s.search.History(...)` / `s.search.Origin(...)` with no `s.search == nil` guard (unlike Search(), which explicitly errors when `s.search` is nil). The diff also removes the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls, so these methods no longer have any gating before dereferencing `s.search`. Since the codebase clearly allows `s.search` to be nil (Search() checks for it), calling History/Origin when search is not configured can nil-pointer panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Moving initWatcher() to run after search.init() opens an unobserved-write window: search.init() builds the index from a DB snapshot, and any writes committed after that snapshot but before initWatcher() starts are never delivered to the index. Resources created/updated while a large index is building (the exact time index building is slow) are permanently missing from the search index until the next restart or rebuild — searches silently return stale results with no error surfaced anywhere; previously the watcher was registered first, so events during the build were captured.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly reorders initialization in `(*server).Init`: previously it started the watcher first (`s.initWatcher()`) and then initialized the search index (`s.search.init(ctx)`); now it runs `s.search.init(ctx)` first and only then starts `s.initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` around the swapped blocks). Given the watcher is described as “watching for changes” and the search init is “initialize the search index”, this creates a clear window during which writes/updates can occur while the index is being built but no watcher is running to observe and feed those changes into the index. The diff shows no compensating mechanism (e.g., buffering/replay) added to close this gap, so missed updates would plausibly leave the search index stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init() is now invoked only from NewResourceServer, converting what was a per-request lazy failure into a hard process-startup failure while the Init() method itself is retained and still public. Operators of deployments where search index init transiently fails (slow DB during startup) now get a server that refuses to boot rather than serving degraded CRUD while retrying init; and any future/alternate constructor path that builds a `server` value without going through NewResourceServer silently serves requests against an uninitialized server (no Init call, no error, watcher never started).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization from per-RPC calls to construction time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure, while the explicit `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` (many blocks deleted). That is a real behavior/operational change worth reviewing (startup can now fail hard if init fails). However, the finding’s claim about previously “retrying init while serving degraded CRUD” isn’t supported by the diff (Init is guarded by `sync.Once` and would not retry after a failure), and the “alternate constructor path” concern isn’t directly verifiable from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the whole-function cacheMu lock from BuildIndex removes the in-flight guard that prevented two concurrent builds for the same key, leaving only the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write protected. Concurrent callers of getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource (e.g., two search requests racing on a cold index) each run a full builder pass against the database and both create a bleve index; the loser's index object is silently discarded and never closed, leaking file handles/memory on the file-backed path, and the winner may be overwritten by the later-finishing stale build (last-write-wins), so searches can serve the older index with no error.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` previously took `b.cacheMu` for the entire function, but the diff removes that whole-function lock and now only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. From the diff alone, this clearly allows two goroutines to concurrently execute the expensive index creation/build path for the same `key` (no in-flight guard remains), and the cache update becomes last-writer-wins. The code also does not close/dispose any previously built `idx` that loses the race, so if concurrent builds occur, one index object can be dropped on the floor without cleanup. Even if the broader call graph isn’t shown, the change in this function itself exposes a real concurrency/correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] On the file-backed path, if the builder callback or any step after `bleve.New(dir, ...)` succeeds but a later step returns an error, the created on-disk bleve index is never closed or cleaned up. Repeated failed builds leave orphaned index directories and open file descriptors under b.opts.Root; the pre-existing `size > FileThreshold` check means large tenants hit this on every retry, eventually exhausting file handles on the server.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go removes a coarse cacheMu lock and only locks around writing b.cache[key] = idx; it does not show the rest of BuildIndex where cleanup/Close might occur on later errors. From the provided hunk alone, we can’t verify that an on-disk bleve index directory is left orphaned or that file descriptors remain open after an error, nor that this behavior is introduced/exposed by this PR.
